chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ali, who said: Humayd ibn Ziyad informed us, from Al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah, who said: Wahb ibn Hafss narrated to me, from Abu Basir and 'Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Seventy thousand angels were assigned to Al-Husayn (peace be upon him); they pray for him, while disheveled and dusty, from the day he was killed until what Allah wills, meaning the rising of the Mahdi. They supplicate for whoever visits him, saying: 'O Lord, these are the visitors of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him); do with them and do for them [what they deserve].'

key_terms.شُعْثًا غُبْرًا: Disheveled and dusty (describing the state of the angels)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the seventy thousand angels praying for Imam Al-Husayn?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the continuous celestial intercession for Imam Al-Husayn (AS), linking his martyrdom directly to the eschatological era of the Mahdi (AJ). The description of the angels as 'disheveled and dusty' (*shuththan ghubran*) emphasizes their active, enduring worship and serves as a spiritual incentive for pilgrims, whose visitation is actively advocated for by these heavenly hosts.
